{{Infobox ancient site |name = Nojikubo Kofun |image = [[File:Nojikubo Kofun, gaikan.jpg|280px]]
Near the explanatory plaque (the mound is located in the forest behind) |alternative_name = |affiliation = |location = {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}{{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma Nojikubo |latitude_deg = 37|latitude_min = 8|latitude_sec = 10.25 |longitude_deg =140|longitude_min = 17|longitude_sec = 10.73 |iso = JP-07 |shape = {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}} |size = |burial_facility = {{ill|Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}} |artifacts = |satellite_tombs = |construction_period = {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} late to {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} early |buried_individual = |imperial_tomb = |historic_sites = National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (Part of {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}) |cultural_properties = |special_notes = |map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Nojikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=10.25|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=10.73|mark=上円下方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Nojikubo Kofun''' (野地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Motonuma, {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Chief Tombs of Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} ! Kofun name ! type ! Burial Facility ! Construction Period |- | {{ill|Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}} || {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} || {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} || {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} late |- | Funada Nakadō Tomb 1 || {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳}} || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} early to mid |- | {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} || Entfun || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |- | '''Nojikubo Kofun''' || {{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}|| Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |}
The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). * == Related Topics == * {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} ** {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} ** {{ill|Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}} == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nojikubo Kofun |image = [[File:Nojikubo Kofun, gaikan.jpg|280px]]
Near the explanatory plaque (the mound is located in the forest behind) |alternative_name = |affiliation = |location = {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}{{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma Nojikubo |latitude_deg = 37|latitude_min = 8|latitude_sec = 10.25 |longitude_deg =140|longitude_min = 17|longitude_sec = 10.73 |iso = JP-07 |shape = {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}} |size = |burial_facility = {{ill|Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}} |artifacts = |satellite_tombs = |construction_period = {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} late to {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} early |buried_individual = |imperial_tomb = |historic_sites = National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (Part of {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}) |cultural_properties = |special_notes = |map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Nojikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=10.25|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=10.73|mark=上円下方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Nojikubo Kofun''' (野地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Motonuma, {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Chief Tombs of Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} ! Kofun name ! type ! Burial Facility ! Construction Period |- | {{ill|Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}} || {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} || {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} || {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} late |- | Funada Nakadō Tomb 1 || {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳}} || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} early to mid |- | {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} || Entfun || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |- | '''Nojikubo Kofun''' || {{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}|| Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |}
The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). * == Related Topics == * {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} ** {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} ** {{ill|Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}} == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == Board of Education}} == External Links == * [http://www.city.shirakawa.fukushima.jp/sp/page/page001388.html Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins > Nojikubo Kofun (Shirakawa City Website)] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nojikubo Kofun |image = [[File:Nojikubo Kofun, gaikan.jpg|280px]]
Near the explanatory plaque (the mound is located in the forest behind) |alternative_name = |affiliation = |location = {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}{{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma Nojikubo |latitude_deg = 37|latitude_min = 8|latitude_sec = 10.25 |longitude_deg =140|longitude_min = 17|longitude_sec = 10.73 |iso = JP-07 |shape = {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}} |size = |burial_facility = {{ill|Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}} |artifacts = |satellite_tombs = |construction_period = {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} late to {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} early |buried_individual = |imperial_tomb = |historic_sites = National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (Part of {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}) |cultural_properties = |special_notes = |map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Nojikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=10.25|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=10.73|mark=上円下方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Nojikubo Kofun''' (野地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Motonuma, {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Chief Tombs of Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} ! Kofun name ! type ! Burial Facility ! Construction Period |- | {{ill|Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}} || {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} || {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} || {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} late |- | Funada Nakadō Tomb 1 || {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳}} || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} early to mid |- | {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} || Entfun || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |- | '''Nojikubo Kofun''' || {{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}|| Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |}
The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). * == Related Topics == * {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} ** {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} ** {{ill|Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}} == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=10.25|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=10.73|mark=上円下方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Nojikubo Kofun''' (野地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Motonuma, {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Chief Tombs of Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} ! Kofun name ! type ! Burial Facility ! Construction Period |- | {{ill|Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}} || {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} || {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} || {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} late |- | Funada Nakadō Tomb 1 || {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳}} || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} early to mid |- | {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} || Entfun || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |- | '''Nojikubo Kofun''' || {{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}|| Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |}
The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=10.25|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=10.73|mark=上円下方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Nojikubo Kofun''' (野地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Motonuma, {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==

The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=10.25|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=10.73|mark=上円下方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Nojikubo Kofun''' (野地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Motonuma, {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Chief Tombs of Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} ! Kofun name ! type ! Burial Facility ! Construction Period |- | {{ill|Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}} || {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} || {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} || {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} late |- | Funada Nakadō Tomb 1 || {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳}} || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} early to mid |- | {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} || Entfun || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |- | '''Nojikubo Kofun''' || {{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}|| Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |}
The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==

The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=10.25|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=10.73|mark=上円下方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Nojikubo Kofun''' (野地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Motonuma, {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Chief Tombs of Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} ! Kofun name ! type ! Burial Facility ! Construction Period |- | {{ill|Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}} || {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} || {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} || {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} late |- | Funada Nakadō Tomb 1 || {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳}} || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} early to mid |- | {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} || Entfun || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |- | '''Nojikubo Kofun''' || {{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}|| Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |}
The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==

The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=10.25|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=10.73|mark=上円下方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Nojikubo Kofun''' (野地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Motonuma, {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Chief Tombs of Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} ! Kofun name ! type ! Burial Facility ! Construction Period |- | {{ill|Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}} || {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} || {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} || {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} late |- | Funada Nakadō Tomb 1 || {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳}} || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} early to mid |- | {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} || Entfun || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |- | '''Nojikubo Kofun''' || {{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}|| Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |}
The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=10.25|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=10.73|mark=上円下方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Nojikubo Kofun''' (野地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Motonuma, {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==

Burial Facility ! Construction Period |- | {{ill|Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}} || {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} || {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} || {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} late |- | Funada Nakadō Tomb 1 || {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳}} || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} early to mid |- | {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} || Entfun || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |- | '''Nojikubo Kofun''' || {{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}|| Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |}
The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. Near the explanatory plaque (the mound is located in the forest behind) |alternative_name = |affiliation = |location = {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}{{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma Nojikubo |latitude_deg = 37|latitude_min = 8|latitude_sec = 10.25 |longitude_deg =140|longitude_min = 17|longitude_sec = 10.73 |iso = JP-07 |shape = {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}} |size = |burial_facility = {{ill|Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}} |artifacts = |satellite_tombs = |construction_period = {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} late to {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} early |buried_individual = |imperial_tomb = |historic_sites = National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (Part of {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}) |cultural_properties = |special_notes = |map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Nojikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=10.25|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=10.73|mark=上円下方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Nojikubo Kofun''' (野地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Motonuma, {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Chief Tombs of Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} ! Kofun name ! type ! Burial Facility ! Construction Period |- | {{ill|Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}} || {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} || {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} || {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} late |- | Funada Nakadō Tomb 1 || {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳}} || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} early to mid |- | {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} || Entfun || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |- | '''Nojikubo Kofun''' || {{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}|| Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |}
The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=10.25|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=10.73|mark=上円下方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Nojikubo Kofun''' (野地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Motonuma, {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Chief Tombs of Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} ! Kofun name ! type ! Burial Facility ! Construction Period |- | {{ill|Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}} || {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} || {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} || {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} late |- | Funada Nakadō Tomb 1 || {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳}} || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} early to mid |- | {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} || Entfun || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |- | '''Nojikubo Kofun''' || {{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}|| Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |}
The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). Near the explanatory plaque (the mound is located in the forest behind) |alternative_name = |affiliation = |location = {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}{{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma Nojikubo |latitude_deg = 37|latitude_min = 8|latitude_sec = 10.25 |longitude_deg =140|longitude_min = 17|longitude_sec = 10.73 |iso = JP-07 |shape = {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}} |size = |burial_facility = {{ill|Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}} |artifacts = |satellite_tombs = |construction_period = {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} late to {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} early |buried_individual = |imperial_tomb = |historic_sites = National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (Part of {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}) |cultural_properties = |special_notes = |map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Nojikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=10.25|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=10.73|mark=上円下方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Nojikubo Kofun''' (野地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Motonuma, {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Chief Tombs of Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} ! Kofun name ! type ! Burial Facility ! Construction Period |- | {{ill|Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}} || {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} || {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} || {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} late |- | Funada Nakadō Tomb 1 || {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳}} || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} early to mid |- | {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} || Entfun || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |- | '''Nojikubo Kofun''' || {{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}|| Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |}
The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==

The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=10.25|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=10.73|mark=上円下方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Nojikubo Kofun''' (野地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Motonuma, {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Chief Tombs of Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} ! Kofun name ! type ! Burial Facility ! Construction Period |- | {{ill|Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}} || {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} || {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} || {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} late |- | Funada Nakadō Tomb 1 || {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳}} || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} early to mid |- | {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} || Entfun || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |- | '''Nojikubo Kofun''' || {{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}|| Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |}
The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==

The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=10.25|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=10.73|mark=上円下方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Nojikubo Kofun''' (野地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Motonuma, {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Chief Tombs of Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} ! Kofun name ! type ! Burial Facility ! Construction Period |- | {{ill|Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}} || {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} || {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} || {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} late |- | Funada Nakadō Tomb 1 || {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳}} || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} early to mid |- | {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} || Entfun || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |- | '''Nojikubo Kofun''' || {{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}|| Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |}
The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==

The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=10.25|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=10.73|mark=上円下方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Nojikubo Kofun''' (野地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Motonuma, {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Chief Tombs of Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} ! Kofun name ! type ! Burial Facility ! Construction Period |- | {{ill|Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}} || {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} || {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} || {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} late |- | Funada Nakadō Tomb 1 || {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳}} || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} early to mid |- | {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} || Entfun || Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |- | '''Nojikubo Kofun''' || {{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}|| Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |}
The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, forming the "Jōen-kahō" shape. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-shape to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Yokoguchi-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Property Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} and was designated a National Historic Site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008年}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic Site designation (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, and it has been designated as a National {{ill|Historic Site|ja|史跡}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==
