The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川|12=draft}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=draft}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀|12=draft}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀|12=draft}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=draft}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|en|lt=Shirakawa District|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川|12=draft}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=draft}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀|12=draft}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀|12=draft}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=draft}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川|12=draft|12=draft}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀|12=draft|12=draft}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀|12=draft|12=draft}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|en|lt=Shirakawa District|12=draft|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群|12=draft|12=draft}} and was Historic site a National Historic site in 2010. == Historical The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川|12=draft|12=draft}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀|12=draft|12=draft}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀|12=draft|12=draft}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|en|lt=Shirakawa District|12=draft|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, and it has been Historic site as a National {{ill|Historic site|ja|史跡|1=Historic site|lt=Historic site of Japan|12=draft|12=draft}}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群|12=draft|12=draft}}." == Overview ==

The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川|12=draft|12=draft}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀|12=draft|12=draft}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀|12=draft|12=draft}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|en|lt=Shirakawa District|12=draft|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群|12=draft|12=draft}} and was Historic site a National Historic site in 2010. == Historical The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川|12=draft|12=draft}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀|12=draft|12=draft}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀|12=draft|12=draft}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|en|lt=Shirakawa District|12=draft|12=draft}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群|12=draft|12=draft}} and was Historic site a National Historic site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008th year|12=draft|12=draft}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic site Historic site (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National {{ill|Historic site|ja|史跡|1=Historic site|lt=Historic site of Japan|12=draft|12=draft}}} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). * == See Also == * 説明板付近（背後の林に墳丘が所在） |別名 = |所属 = |所在地 = [[福島県]][[白河市]]本沼野地久保 |緯度度 = 37|緯度分 = 8|緯度秒 = 10.25 |経度度 =140|経度分 = 17|経度秒 = 10.73 |ISO = JP-07 |形状 = [[上円下方墳]] |規模 = |埋葬施設 = [[横口式石槨]] |出土品 = |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[7世紀]]後半-[[8世紀]]初頭 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = 国の[[史跡]]「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」に包含 |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = |地図2 = {{Location map|Japan Fukushima|label=野地久保
古墳|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=10.25|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=10.73|mark=上円下方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''野地久保古墳'''（のじくぼこふん）は、[[福島県]][[白河市]]本沼（もとぬま）にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[上円下方墳]]。国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」のうち）。 == 概要 ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+白河地域の首長墓{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}} !古墳名 !形状 !埋葬施設 !築造時期 |- |[[下総塚古墳]]||[[前方後円墳]]||[[横穴式石室]]||[[6世紀]]後半 |- |舟田中道1号墳||[[円墳]]||横穴式石室||[[7世紀]]前半-7世紀中葉 |- |[[谷地久保古墳]]||円墳||[[横口式石槨]]||7世紀後半-[[8世紀]]初頭 |- |'''野地久保古墳'''||[[上円下方墳]]||横口式石槨||7世紀後半-8世紀初頭 |}
福島県南部、[[阿武隈川]]左岸の丘陵南東斜面に築造された古墳である。[[谷地久保古墳]]と同じ谷の南東400メートルに位置する。これまでに墳丘上部・東半が削平を受けているほか、[[2008年]]（[[平成]]20年）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳丘は2段築成。墳形は1段目が方形で2段目が円形の上円下方形で、1段目は一辺16メートル、2段目は直径約10メートルを測る。墳丘斜面には川原石による積石が、平坦面には円礫による貼石が認められる{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。また墳丘周囲には掘割状の外周溝状遺構が認められる{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。埋葬施設は[[横口式石槨]]である。床石1石のみが原位置を保って遺存しており、他に4石が周辺に散在する{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。石槨の前庭部は南にハ字形に開き、壁面には川原石を小口積みに、底面には小円礫を敷設する{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。盗掘に遭っているため副葬品は詳らかでない{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 この野地久保古墳は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]後半-[[8世紀]]初頭頃の築造と推定される{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。全国でも数少ない上円下方墳の1つとして注目されるほか、北西の谷地久保古墳とともに畿内的な横口式石槨を有する特異な古墳であり、被葬者は古代[[白河郡]]における盟主的な立場の人物と推定される{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。また、南方に所在する[[下総塚古墳]]（後期の首長墓）と舟田中道遺跡（後期の豪族居館）とともに古墳時代の[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]として認知され、周辺に展開する[[関和久官衙遺跡]]（推定白河郡衙跡）・[[借宿廃寺跡]]からなる古代の白河官衙遺跡群と合わせて、古代白河郡の中心地を示す遺跡群の一角として重要視される古墳である。 古墳域は[[2010年]]（平成22年）に国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「白河舟田・本沼遺跡群」に追加指定）。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[2008年]]（平成20年）、国の史跡指定に向けた発掘調査（白河市教育委員会、[[2010年]]に報告書刊行）。 * 2010年（平成22年）8月5日、国の[[史跡]]に指定（史跡「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」に追加指定）。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 史跡説明板（白河市教育委員会設置） * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2011|chapter=|title=国指定史跡 白河舟田・本沼遺跡群 白河官衙遺跡群（白河市文化財パンフレット）|publisher=白河市教育委員会|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}}} == 関連文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=鈴木功|year=2006|chapter=|title=白河郡衙遺跡群 -古代東国行政の一大中心地-（日本の遺跡10）|publisher=[[同成社]]|isbn=4886213545|ref=}} * {{Cite journal|和書|author=鈴木功・鈴木一寿|title=野地久保古墳の調査|date=2009|publisher=ニュー・サイエンス社|journal=月刊考古学ジャーナル|volume=|number=592|pages=25-29|url=|doi=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2010|chapter=|title=野地久保古墳確認調査報告書（白河市埋蔵文化財調査報告書 第52集）|publisher=白河市教育委員会|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2017|chapter=|title=史跡白河舟田・本沼遺跡群、白河官衙遺跡群保存活用計画書|publisher=白河市教育委員会|isbn=|ref=}} == 関連項目 == * [[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]] ** [[谷地久保古墳]] ** [[下総塚古墳]] == 外部リンク == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|00003447|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} * [http://www.city.shirakawa.fukushima.jp/sp/page/page001388.html 白河舟田・本沼遺跡群 > 野地久保古墳] - 白河市ホームページ {{DEFAULTSORT:のしくほこふん}} [[Category:福島県の古墳]] This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳}} |name = Nojikubo Kofun |image = [[File:Nojikubo Kofun, gaikan.jpg|280px]]
Near the explanatory plaque (the mound is located in the forest behind) |alternate_name = |affiliation = |location = {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}{{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma Nojikubo |coordinates = 37|coordinates = 8|coordinates = 10.25 |coordinates =140|coordinates = 17|coordinates = 10.73 |iso = JP-07 |type = {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}} |size = |burial = {{ill|Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}} |burial goods = |satellite_tombs = |built = {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} late to {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} early |Interred_individual = |imperial_tomb = |historic_sites = National {{ill|Historic site|ja|史跡|1=Historic site|lt=Historic site of Japan}}} (Part of {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}) |cultural_properties = |special_notes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|map_dot_label=Nojikubo
Kofun|coordinates=37|coordinates=8|coordinates=10.25|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=10.73|mark=上円下方墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Nojikubo Kofun''' (野地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Motonuma, {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}}, and it has been Historic site as a National {{ill|Historic site|ja|史跡|1=Historic site|lt=Historic site of Japan}}} as part of the "{{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}." == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Chief Tombs of Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} ! Kofun name ! type ! burial ! built |- | {{ill|Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}} || {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} || {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} late |- | Funada Nakadō Tomb 1 || {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku || {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} early to mid |- | {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} || Entfun || Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |- | '''Nojikubo Kofun''' || {{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}|| Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku || 7th century late to 8th century early |}
The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川|qq=draft}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀|qq=draft}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀|qq=draft}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|en|lt=Shirakawa District|qq=draft}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群|qq=draft}} and was Historic site a National Historic site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/7th century|qq=}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/8th century|qq=}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|en|lt=Shirakawa District|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|qq=}} and was Historic site a National Historic site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|ja|2008th The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abukuma River|qq=}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/7th century|qq=}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/8th century|qq=}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōen-kahō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=}}, and it has been Historic site as a National [[:en:Historic site|Historic site of Japan]]} as part of the "[[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins]]." == Overview ==

The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]] in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] to early [[:en:8th century|8th century]] and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]].{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins]] and was Historic site a National Historic site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * [[:en:2008|2008]]: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic site Historic site (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National [[:en:Historic site|Historic site of The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]] in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] to early [[:en:8th century|8th century]] and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]].{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins]] and was Historic site a National Historic site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * [[:en:2008|2008]]: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic site Historic site (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National [[:en:Historic site|Historic site of It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] to early [[:en:8th century|8th century]] and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]] in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] to early [[:en:8th century|8th century]] and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]].{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins]] and was Historic site a National Historic site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * [[:en:2008|2008]]: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic site Historic site (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National [[:en:Historic site|Historic site of The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]] in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] to early [[:en:8th century|8th century]] and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]].{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]] in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] to early [[:en:8th century|8th century]] and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]].{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins]] and was Historic site a National Historic site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * [[:en:2008|2008]]: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic site Historic site (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National [[:en:Historic site|Historic site of Japan]]} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). * == See Also == * [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites]] ** {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} ** {{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|lt=Shimosozuka Kofun|lt=Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosōzuka Kofun|qq=}} == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|year=2011|title=Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins: Shirakawa Government Office Ruins (Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet)|publisher=Shirakawa City Board of Education}} == External Links == * [http://www.city.shirakawa.fukushima.jp/sp/page/page001388.html Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins > Nojikubo Kofun (Shirakawa City Website)] {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|野地久保古墳|version=99995299|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Completion tier 4]] [[Category:Joenkahofun]] }} [[sn:Nojikubo Kofun]] [[ja:野地久保古墳]] [[Category:National historic sites in Fukushima prefecture]] [[Category:Kofun of Fukushima prefecture]]

The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]] in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] to early [[:en:8th century|8th century]] and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]].{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins]] and was Historic site a National Historic site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * [[:en:2008|2008]]: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic site Historic site (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National [[:en:Historic site|Historic site of Japan]]} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). * == See Also == * [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites]] ** {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} ** {{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|lt=Shimosozuka Kofun|lt=Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosōzuka Kofun|qq=}} == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|year=2011|title=Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins: Shirakawa Government Office Ruins (Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet)|publisher=Shirakawa City Board of Education}} == External Links == * [http://www.city.shirakawa.fukushima.jp/sp/page/page001388.html Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins > Nojikubo Kofun (Shirakawa City Website)] {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|野地久保古墳|version=99995299|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Completion tier 4]] [[Category:Joenkahofun]] }} [[ja:野地久保古墳]] [[Category:National historic sites in Fukushima prefecture]] [[Category:Kofun of Fukushima prefecture]] {{wikidata link|Q109597323}}

The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]] in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] to early [[:en:8th century|8th century]] and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]].{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins]] and was Historic site a National Historic site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * [[:en:2008|2008]]: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic site Historic site (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National [[:en:Historic site|Historic site of Japan]]} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). * == See Also == * [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites]] ** {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} ** {{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|lt=Shimosozuka Kofun|lt=Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosōzuka Kofun|qq=}} == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|year=2011|title=Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins: Shirakawa Government Office Ruins (Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet)|publisher=Shirakawa City Board of Education}} == External Links == * [http://www.city.shirakawa.fukushima.jp/sp/page/page001388.html Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins > Nojikubo Kofun (Shirakawa City Website)] {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|野地久保古墳|version=99995299|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Completion tier 4]] [[Category:Joenkahofun]] }} [[ja:野地久保古墳]] [[Category:National historic sites in Fukushima prefecture]] [[Category:Kofun of Fukushima prefecture]] {{wikidata link|Q109597323}} [[Category:Wikidata no short description]]

The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]] in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] to early [[:en:8th century|8th century]] and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]].{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins]] and was Historic site a National Historic site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * [[:en:2008|2008]]: Excavation The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]] in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] to early [[:en:8th century|8th century]] and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]].{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins]] and was Historic site a National Historic site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * [[:en:2008|2008]]: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic site Historic site (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated as a National [[:en:Historic site|Historic site of Japan]]} (added to the Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins). * == See Also == * [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites]] ** {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} ** {{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|lt=Shimosozuka Kofun|lt=Shimosōzuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosōzuka Kofun|qq=}} == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|year=2011|title=Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins: Shirakawa Government Office Ruins (Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet)|publisher=Shirakawa City Board of Education}} == External Links == * [http://www.city.shirakawa.fukushima.jp/sp/page/page001388.html Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins > Nojikubo Kofun (Shirakawa City Website)] {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|野地久保古墳|version=99995299|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| }} [[ja:野地久保古墳]] {{wikidata link|Q109597323}} [[Category:Completion tier 4]] [[Category:Joenkahofun]] [[Category:Kofun of Fukushima prefecture]] [[Category:National historic sites in Fukushima prefecture]] [[Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] [[Category:Wikidata no short description]]

The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|en|Abukuma River|WD=Q335853|lt=Abukuma River}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} to early {{ill|8th century|en|8th century|WD=Q8086|lt=8th century}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|en|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|WD=Q1155789|lt=Shirakawa District}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|en|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|WD=Q11579979|lt=Shirakawa Funada Motonuma The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|en|Abukuma River|WD=Q335853|lt=Abukuma River}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} to early {{ill|8th century|en|8th century|WD=Q8086|lt=8th century}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}, it features a distinctive Cave Tomb-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|en|Abukuma River|WD=Q335853|lt=Abukuma River|1=Abukuma River}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoanabo-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century|1=7th century}} to early {{ill|8th century|en|8th century|WD=Q8086|lt=8th century|1=8th century}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}, it features a distinctive Yokoanabo-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|en|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|WD=Q1155789|lt=Shirakawa District|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|en|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|WD=Q11579979|lt=Shirakawa Funada Motonuma Ruins|1=Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites}} and was Historic site a National Historic site in 2010. == Historical Timeline == * {{ill|2008|en|2008|WD=Q2004|lt=2008|1=2008}}: Excavation survey by Shirakawa City Board of Education for national Historic site Historic site (report published in 2010). * 2010 (Heisei 22): Designated The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|en|Abukuma River|WD=Q335853|lt=Abukuma River|1=Abukuma River}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. The kofun is located on the southeastern slope of a hill on the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|en|Abukuma River|WD=Q335853|lt=Abukuma River|1=Abukuma River}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture. It lies 400 meters southeast of {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}} in the same valley. The upper and eastern parts of the mound have been flattened, and an excavation survey was conducted in 2008. The mound is constructed in two tiers. The first tier is square (16 meters on each side), while the second tier is circular with a diameter of approximately 10 meters, typeing the "Jōen-kahō" type. The slopes of the mound feature a stone-pile construction using river stones, and the flat areas are covered with gravel paving.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Surrounding the mound is a trench-like outer moat structure. The burial facility is a Yokoanabo-shiki sekaku. While only the floor stone remains in its original position, four other stones are scattered nearby.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The front yard of the burial chamber opens in a V-type to the south, with walls made of upright river stones and the floor paved with gravel.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Due to looting, the accompanying grave goods are not well-documented.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} Nojikubo Kofun is dated to the late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century|1=7th century}} to early {{ill|8th century|en|8th century|WD=Q8086|lt=8th century|1=8th century}} and is recognized as one of the few remaining examples of a Jōen-kahō-fun. Along with {{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}, it features a distinctive Yokoanabo-shiki sekaku, characteristic of the Yamato region. The tomb's occupant is presumed to have been a prominent leader in the ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|en|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|WD=Q1155789|lt=Shirakawa District|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima}}.{{Sfn|Shirakawa City designation1 Pamphlet|2011}} The kofun is part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|en|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma
